path: PATH 1: training frontier LMs from scratch (pretraining and mid-training)

items.title: Fantastic Pretraining Optimizers and Where to Find Them
items.one_sentence_method: Coordinate-descent hyperparameter tuning of 11 optimizers (AdamW, NAdamW, MARS, Cautious, Lion, Adam-mini, Muon, Scion, Kron/PSGD, SOAP, Sophia) across 0.1B-1.2B and 1-8x Chinchilla, with end-of-training evaluation.
items.headline_claim: Matrix-preconditioned optimizers give at most 1.4x over well-tuned AdamW at 0.1B, decaying to ~1.1x at 1.2B; Soap/Kron overtake Muon at >=8x Chinchilla; a fitted scaling law predicts Muon slightly worse than AdamW at 7B/1x Chinchilla.
items.path_relevance: Definitive benchmark for optimizer choice in from-scratch pretraining; sets the fair-comparison protocol.
items.known_frontier_adoption: None (benchmark); cites Kimi K2 (MuonClip) and GLM-4.5 as the only frontier Muon adopters.

items.title: Hyperparameter Transfer Enables Consistent Gains of Matrix-Preconditioned Optimizers Across Scales
items.one_sentence_method: Derives muP width/depth (CompleteP-style) scaling rules for Shampoo, SOAP and Muon including blocking/grafting, plus 1/width independent weight decay; blocking and explicit spectral normalization fix finite-width drift.
items.headline_claim: Muon, SOAP and Shampoo keep a consistent ~1.4x speedup over AdamW from 190M to 1.4B only under correct transfer; under standard parameterization the speedup vanishes with scale.
items.path_relevance: Seed paper: shows optimizer gains at scale are conditional on parameterization; compute-optimal model size is larger for matrix optimizers.

items.title: Don't be lazy: CompleteP enables compute-efficient deep transformers
items.affiliations: Cerebras Systems; ETH Zurich; Princeton; Harvard
items.one_sentence_method: Depth parameterization with alpha=1 residual-branch scaling (1/L) plus LN, bias, epsilon and weight-decay rescaling that yields depth-wise HP transfer and non-lazy (complete) feature learning in all layers.
items.largest_scale_tested: 1.9B total (1.5B non-embedding), 2-128 layers, 20 TPP compute-optimal on CS-3
items.headline_claim: 12-34% FLOP savings over muP (11.8% at optimal shape, 34.4% for 179-layer models); HP transfer from 2 to 128 layers.
items.path_relevance: Depth-muP for scaling deep frontier models; used by 2512.05620 as the depth rule for matrix optimizers.
items.known_frontier_adoption: None named; authors plan SOTA-scale runs.

items.title: Power Lines: Scaling Laws for Weight Decay and Batch Size in LLM Pre-training
items.tier_evidence: OpenReview venue line 'NeurIPS 2025 poster' (forum bFXbLQzRoZ); proceedings PDF papers.nips.cc/.../b5f78a17a94da3e34c935515d1b6adae-Paper-Conference.pdf
items.one_sentence_method: Fits power laws for the AdamW timescale tau=B/(eta*lambda*D) in tokens-per-parameter and for optimal/critical batch size in D using hundreds of muP-trained models.
items.largest_scale_tested: Hundreds of muP models, TPP 20-1280; models up to ~1B
items.headline_claim: Optimal tau follows a power law in D/N (predicts lambda_opt); B_opt ~ D^0.4 and B_crit ~ D^0.5 independent of N; fixed weight decay distorts batch-size laws.
items.path_relevance: Weight-decay and batch-size scaling for frontier runs.

items.title: A Multi-Power Law for Loss Curve Prediction Across Learning Rate Schedules
items.one_sentence_method: Empirical multi-power law predicting the whole loss curve from the LR schedule (sum of LRs plus LR-decay correction), fitted from <=3 runs, then used to optimize the schedule.
items.headline_claim: Predicts unseen schedules; optimized schedule is WSD-like and beats cosine by >0.02 loss and beats grid-tuned WSD.
items.path_relevance: Scaling-law-aware LR schedules; justifies WSD-style schedules used by frontier labs.
items.known_frontier_adoption: WSD itself used by Kimi K2, LLaDA, NVFP4 runs (not this law).

items.title: Straight to Zero: Why Linearly Decaying the Learning Rate to Zero Works Best for LLMs
items.one_sentence_method: Large-scale comparison of LR schedules under tuned peak LR, with an EMA-of-updates interpretation of AdamW explaining linear decay-to-zero.
items.headline_claim: Linear D2Z beats cosine/10x decay and WSD; a 610M model at 80 TPP with D2Z beats 200 TPP with 10x decay (~60% compute savings); benefits grow with TPP.
items.path_relevance: LR-schedule choice for over-trained frontier models.

items.title: Scaling Collapse Reveals Universal Dynamics in Compute-Optimally Trained Neural Networks
items.tier_evidence: PMLR v267:50697-50720 (ICML 2025); ICML 2025 oral page icml.cc/virtual/2025/oral/47243
items.one_sentence_method: Shows compute-optimal loss curves collapse onto one universal curve after normalizing compute and loss; LR decay gives 'supercollapse' below seed noise; a quadratic SGD-noise model explains it.
items.largest_scale_tested: Transformers on next-token prediction (CIFAR-5M and text), multiple sizes
items.headline_claim: Collapse breaks when LR or data scaling is suboptimal, giving a cheap diagnostic of correct hyperparameter scaling.
items.path_relevance: Diagnostic for correct HP scaling in telescoping sweeps.

items.title: Training Deep Learning Models with Norm-Constrained LMOs (Scion)
items.one_sentence_method: Stochastic conditional-gradient family using linear-minimization oracles over layer-wise operator-norm balls, unifying Muon/Adam-like updates; Scion needs no Adam and only one weight + one gradient copy.
items.largest_scale_tested: nanoGPT up to 3B; ViT on ImageNet
items.headline_claim: Zero-shot HP transfer and better large-batch tolerance; first provable rate for Muon with/without weight decay.
items.path_relevance: Spectral steepest-descent framing of Muon; memory-light optimizer.
items.known_frontier_adoption: Used as the 'Scion' baseline implementation in Fantastic Optimizers and SAMuon.

items.title: The Polar Express: Optimal Matrix Sign Methods and Their Application to the Muon Algorithm
items.tier_evidence: OpenReview PDF header 'Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2026' (forum yRtgZ1K8hO)
items.one_sentence_method: Minimax-optimal per-iteration polynomial update for the polar factor (replacing Newton-Schulz) with bfloat16-safe modifications.
items.headline_claim: Consistent validation-loss gains over Newton-Schulz and Jordan/You polynomials across learning rates; converges ~2x faster than NS; adopted in the NanoGPT speedrun.
items.path_relevance: Newton-Schulz scaling/accuracy study for Muon.
items.known_frontier_adoption: NanoGPT speedrun; no frontier report names it.

items.title: NorMuon: Making Muon more efficient and scalable
items.tier_evidence: Microsoft Research publication page lists venue 'ICML 2026'
items.one_sentence_method: Adds neuron-wise (row) second-moment normalization after Muon's orthogonalization and an FSDP2 distributed implementation that shards orthogonalization work.
items.headline_claim: 21.74% better training efficiency than Adam and 11.31% over Muon at 1.1B; 13.91% at 5.4B.
items.path_relevance: Distributed Muon variant combining adaptive LR with orthogonalization.
items.known_frontier_adoption: Shipped in microsoft/dion repo; no frontier report.

items.title: When and Why Grouping Attention Heads Accelerates Muon Optimization (Group Muon)
items.one_sentence_method: One-step descent analysis of full-matrix vs head-grouped Muon (whitening gain vs grouping-induced norm cost); proposes head group size and grouping rule as optimizer hyperparameters.
items.headline_claim: Random Q/K grouping with 6 heads per group beats both full-QKV Muon and fully head-wise MuonSplit; head-wise wins early but is overtaken later.
items.path_relevance: Per-head Muon design; explains GLM-5's MuonSplit choice.
items.known_frontier_adoption: GLM-5 (MuonSplit, per this paper); modded-nanoGPT record.

items.title: Parameters vs FLOPs: Scaling Laws for Optimal Sparsity for Mixture-of-Experts Language Models
items.one_sentence_method: IsoFLOP sweeps over MoE sparsity S=(E-K)/E with a parametric loss law L(N,D,S) including an N-S interaction term.
items.largest_scale_tested: Models up to ~26B total params; budgets 3e19-1e21 FLOPs
items.headline_claim: For fixed compute the optimal sparsity rises with total parameters and approaches 1; denser models transfer better to reasoning-style downstream tasks.
items.path_relevance: MoE scaling laws / optimal sparsity.

items.title: Joint MoE Scaling Laws: Mixture of Experts Can Be Memory Efficient
items.one_sentence_method: Joint dense/MoE scaling law in active params, tokens and expert count with memory and inference constraints.
items.headline_claim: MoE can be memory-optimal: a total-parameter-matched MoE beats an overtrained dense model at equal compute; optimal expert count depends on memory budget.
items.path_relevance: MoE configuration under compute+memory budgets.

items.title: Towards Greater Leverage: Scaling Laws for Efficient Mixture-of-Experts Language Models
items.one_sentence_method: Defines Efficiency Leverage (compute ratio of dense model matching an MoE) and fits EL(A,G,C) as power law in activation ratio and compute with log-polynomial granularity term.
items.largest_scale_tested: 300+ MoE models up to 28B; Ling-mini-beta 17.5B/0.85B active on 1T tokens
items.headline_claim: Predicted >7x leverage at 3.1% activation and granularity 12; Ling-mini-beta matched a 6.1B dense model with >7x less compute.
items.path_relevance: Ultra-sparse MoE design laws.

items.title: Predictable Scale: Part II, Farseer: A Refined Scaling Law in Large Language Models
items.one_sentence_method: Loss-surface law L(N,D) with N-dependent data exponent fitted by differential piecewise, multi-round iterative fitting on ~1,000 trained LLMs.
items.headline_claim: Extrapolation error 0.50% vs 2.68% for Chinchilla (433% higher); optimal D/N rises with compute; small-scale mixture conclusions can reverse at scale.
items.path_relevance: Loss-surface laws for ablating recipes before frontier runs.

items.title: Scaling Laws for Optimal Data Mixtures
items.one_sentence_method: Additive and joint scaling laws L(N,D,h) over domain weights h, fitted on small runs and minimized on the simplex via mirror descent.
items.largest_scale_tested: 7B models on 150B tokens (LLM); also NMM and LVM
items.headline_claim: Small-scale fits predict loss at 8B and unseen mixtures; law-derived weights beat token-proportional and uniform mixtures downstream.
items.path_relevance: RegMix successor: data-mixing laws that extrapolate across scale.

items.title: Pre-training under infinite compute
items.tier_evidence: ICLR 2026 proceedings PDF proceedings.iclr.cc/.../79682ef54677a2cb3dfb8383b372037f-Paper-Conference.pdf; ICLR 2026 oral page 10008474
items.one_sentence_method: Data-constrained recipe: tune weight decay (30x standard), epochs and parameters per size, then ensemble independent models and evaluate by scaling-law asymptote.
items.largest_scale_tested: 200M-token seed corpus; models to 1.4B; ensembles of five 1.4B
items.headline_claim: Joint recipe reaches the 200M-token asymptote with 5.17x less data; distilled 8x-smaller student keeps 83% of ensemble gain; 17.5x data efficiency on math mid-training.
items.path_relevance: Data-constrained scaling and regularization for pretraining.

items.title: Diffusion Beats Autoregressive in Data-Constrained Settings
items.one_sentence_method: Trains 100 masked-diffusion and 100 AR models over unique-token budgets, sizes and epochs; fits Muennighoff-style data-constrained laws.
items.headline_claim: Diffusion R*_D ~ 500 epochs vs ~15-30 for AR; critical compute where diffusion wins scales as U^2.174; masking acts as implicit ordering augmentation.
items.path_relevance: Objective choice under data constraints.

items.title: Scaling Laws for Floating-Point Quantization Training
items.one_sentence_method: 'Capybara' law adding a D^beta/N^alpha * log2(B)/(E,M) term for exponent, mantissa and scaling block size to Chinchilla.
items.largest_scale_tested: Several hundred runs (sizes not stated in abstract)
items.headline_claim: Optimal layouts E2M1/E4M3/E8M7; a critical data size beyond which low-precision loss rises; best cost-performance precision 4-8 bits.
items.path_relevance: Precision-aware scaling law for FP8/FP4 pretraining.

items.title: Quartet: Native FP4 Training Can Be Optimal for Large Language Models
items.one_sentence_method: End-to-end MXFP4 training (Hadamard + QuEST forward, stochastic-rounding backward) with a low-precision scaling law over forward/backward precision and Blackwell kernels.
items.largest_scale_tested: Llama 30M-1.6B (law), 7B stability run, D/N up to 100
items.headline_claim: MXFP4 near-lossless in large-data regime; ~2x FP8 GEMM speed; ~15% fewer params and 5x less data than LUQ-INT4 at equal loss.
items.path_relevance: FP4 pretraining from scratch.

items.title: Scaling Law for Quantization-Aware Training
items.tier_evidence: ICML 2026 poster page icml.cc/virtual/2026/poster/62561; OpenReview dcPH77OVgN
items.one_sentence_method: Unified W4A4 QAT law: error = k * D^gD * (log2 G)^gG / N^gN, decomposed into weight and activation components.
items.headline_claim: Error falls with N but rises with tokens and coarser groups; FC2 activation outliers dominate; 8-bit FC2 inputs cut error 20-43%.
items.path_relevance: Quantization-aware pretraining scaling.

items.title: Distillation Scaling Laws
items.one_sentence_method: Scaling law for student cross-entropy as a function of student size/tokens and teacher cross-entropy, with compute-optimal allocation recipes.
items.headline_claim: Distillation beats supervised pretraining only below a student-size-dependent compute threshold and only if the teacher already exists; otherwise supervised wins.
items.path_relevance: Pretraining-side compute allocation between distillation and from-scratch training.

items.title: Native Sparse Attention: Hardware-Aligned and Natively Trainable Sparse Attention
items.one_sentence_method: Three-path attention (compressed tokens, selected fine-grained blocks, sliding window) with Triton kernels, trained end-to-end from scratch.
items.headline_claim: Matches or beats full attention on 7/9 general benchmarks and on LongBench; 9.0x forward / 6.0x backward speedup at 64k.
items.path_relevance: Sparse attention trained from scratch.

items.title: MoBA: Mixture of Block Attention for Long-Context LLMs
items.one_sentence_method: MoE-style parameter-free top-k gating of query tokens to KV blocks; switches between full and sparse attention.
items.largest_scale_tested: Llama-8B continued to 1M context; 10M-token scaling test
items.headline_claim: Comparable to full attention with 6.5x prefill speedup at 1M and 16x at 10M; deployed for Kimi long-context.
items.path_relevance: Sparse attention for long-context pretraining/mid-training.

items.title: Gated Attention for Large Language Models: Non-linearity, Sparsity, and Attention-Sink-Free
items.tier_evidence: NeurIPS 2025 proceedings 904e89bb4e632e75fb47f093b620b257; repo notes NeurIPS 2025 Oral and Best Paper Award
items.one_sentence_method: Head-specific sigmoid gate on the SDPA output, compared against 30 gating variants.
items.headline_claim: ~0.2 PPL and +2 MMLU, near-elimination of loss spikes, no attention sink, +10 RULER; enables larger LRs.
items.path_relevance: Attention-block change that improves stability and scaling.

items.title: Rope to Nope and Back Again: A New Hybrid Attention Strategy
items.one_sentence_method: Interleaves NoPE full-attention layers with RoPE sliding-window layers (RNoPE-SWA) based on attention-mass analysis.
items.headline_claim: Beats RoPE full attention on long and short context with ~4x smaller KV cache and no RoPE scaling; RoPE/NoPE layers self-specialize into local vs retrieval roles.
items.path_relevance: NoPE and position-encoding design for from-scratch long-context models.

items.title: Mamba-3: Improved Sequence Modeling using State Space Principles
items.affiliations: CMU; Princeton; Together AI; Cartesia AI
items.tier_evidence: ICLR 2026 oral page iclr.cc/virtual/2026/oral/10010353; OpenReview HwCvaJOiCj
items.one_sentence_method: Exponential-trapezoidal discretization, complex-valued (data-dependent rotary) state transitions for state tracking, and MIMO state update.
items.largest_scale_tested: 1.5B on 100B FineWeb-Edu tokens; hybrids at 5:1 with NoPE attention
items.headline_claim: +0.6 avg accuracy over Gated DeltaNet (SISO), +1.8 with MIMO; matches Mamba-2 perplexity at half the state size.
items.path_relevance: Linear-attention/SSM primitive for hybrid frontier models.

items.title: RWKV-7 "Goose" with Expressive Dynamic State Evolution
items.tier_evidence: COLM 2025 accepted papers list (colmweb.org/2025/AcceptedPapers.html); OpenReview rl8H9BWjNO
items.one_sentence_method: Generalized delta rule with vector-valued decay, vector in-context learning rates and decoupled removal/replacement keys.
items.headline_claim: New 3B SoTA on multilingual tasks; proven to recognize all regular languages (beyond TC0) with constant layers.
items.path_relevance: Attention-free architecture trained from scratch.

items.title: Titans: Learning to Memorize at Test Time
items.tier_evidence: NeurIPS 2025 proceedings PDF a4ca07aa108036f80cbb5b82285fd4b1; neurips.cc poster 119639
items.one_sentence_method: Neural long-term memory module trained at test time via surprise-gated gradient updates, combined with attention (MAC/MAG/MAL variants).
items.largest_scale_tested: Up to 760M params; NIAH beyond 2M context
items.headline_claim: Outperforms Transformer and linear-recurrent baselines on LM and reasoning and scales to >2M-token needle tasks.
items.path_relevance: Memory-layer / test-time-training architecture (in window: v1 2024-12-31).

items.title: Large Language Diffusion Models (LLaDA)
items.affiliations: Renmin University of China; Ant Group
items.one_sentence_method: Masked diffusion LM trained from scratch with random masking ratio, WSD schedule, then SFT.
items.headline_claim: Competitive with LLaMA3 8B in in-context learning; solves reversal-curse poem completion better than GPT-4o.
items.path_relevance: Diffusion LM pretraining from random init.

items.title: Model Merging in Pre-training of Large Language Models (PMA)
items.one_sentence_method: Pre-trained Model Averaging of checkpoints from the constant-LR phase of WSD, plus PMA-init for recovering from loss spikes.
items.headline_claim: Merged constant-LR checkpoints match or beat annealed models and predict annealing (HumanEval 54.3->61.6 on 10B/100B MoE).
items.path_relevance: Checkpoint averaging as a pretraining tool.
items.known_frontier_adoption: ByteDance Seed (in-house); DeepSeek-V3 and Llama 3.1 mention merging.

items.title: L-MTP: Leap Multi-Token Prediction Beyond Adjacent Context for Large Language Models
items.one_sentence_method: MTP heads predict non-adjacent (leap) future tokens; decoding reuses overlapping context for speedup.
items.headline_claim: Outperforms MTP on most math/code tasks with 22% more speedup at equal heads; up to 4x with speculative decoding.
items.path_relevance: MTP objective variant (note: mostly head-adaptation, not from-scratch).

items.title: Pre-Training Curriculum for Multi-Token Prediction in Language Models
items.one_sentence_method: Forward (NTP->MTP) and reverse (MTP->NTP) curricula over number of predicted tokens during pretraining of small LMs.
items.headline_claim: Forward curriculum lets small models benefit from MTP while keeping self-speculative decoding; reverse gives best NTP quality but no decoding speedup.
items.path_relevance: MTP from scratch at small scale.

items.title: Demons in the Detail: On Implementing Load Balancing Loss for Training Specialized Mixture-of-Expert Models
items.one_sentence_method: Computes the MoE load-balancing loss over the global batch (synchronizing expert frequencies) instead of per micro-batch.
items.largest_scale_tested: MoE up to 42.8B total on 400B tokens
items.headline_claim: ~0.1 lower PPL and ~2 points on benchmarks, with emergent domain specialization; <3% latency; used in Qwen3-MoE.
items.path_relevance: MoE routing / load balancing for ultra-sparse frontier MoEs.

items.title: Conditional Memory via Scalable Lookup: A New Axis of Sparsity for Large Language Models (Engram)
items.one_sentence_method: Hashed n-gram embedding lookup module with context-aware gating added to an MoE backbone; a U-shaped sparsity-allocation law splits parameters between experts and memory.
items.headline_claim: +3.4 MMLU, +5.0 BBH, +3.0 HumanEval, Multi-Query NIAH 84.2->97.0; 100B-parameter table offloaded to host with <3% overhead.
items.path_relevance: Memory/lookup layers as a new sparsity axis.

items.title: Midtraining Bridges Pretraining and Posttraining Distributions
items.one_sentence_method: Controlled from-scratch pretraining with a mid-training phase varying domain, start time and mixture weight, evaluated after SFT.
items.headline_claim: Mid-training helps most for code/math; timing and mixture weight interact (early start tolerates 80% specialized data, late start needs ~10%); beats continued pretraining and reduces forgetting.
items.path_relevance: Mid-training data schedules.
items.known_frontier_adoption: None named (practice used by OLMo, Llama, Kimi).

items.title: LLM-JEPA: Large Language Models Meet Joint Embedding Predictive Architectures
items.tier_evidence: ICLR 2026 (OpenReview forum GbXKPo9QfH; secondary paper-note lists ICLR 2026)
items.one_sentence_method: Adds a cosine JEPA loss between Pred(Enc(Text)) and Enc(Code) views to the next-token objective, reusing LLM weights as encoder/predictor.
items.largest_scale_tested: 1B-8B fine-tuning; 1B pretraining from random init on NL-RX-SYNTH
items.headline_claim: Pretraining accuracy 54.38->60.59; large fine-tuning gains; overfitting resistance; ~2x training compute overhead.
items.path_relevance: JEPA-style objective for LM pretraining (small-scale evidence).

items.title: Energy-Based Transformers are Scalable Learners and Thinkers
items.one_sentence_method: Energy-based transformer trained to score input/prediction pairs; predictions via gradient-descent energy minimization; landscape regularizers.
items.headline_claim: Up to 35% higher scaling rate than Transformer++ across data, batch, params, FLOPs and depth; 29% larger gains from inference-time thinking.
items.path_relevance: Energy-based LM objective from scratch.

items.title: RLP: Reinforcement as a Pretraining Objective
items.tier_evidence: ICLR 2026 proceedings PDF 44a45e27879b8fbab6e123ad8b93afc2; NVIDIA research page 'ICLR 2026'
items.one_sentence_method: Verifier-free information-gain reward: sample a chain-of-thought before each token and reward the log-likelihood gain over an EMA no-think baseline, trained with group-relative clipped updates during late pretraining.
items.headline_claim: +19% average on 8 math/science benchmarks at 1.7B; 42.81->61.32 on 12B; beats RPT by ~4 points and compute-matched NTP with 35x more data.
items.path_relevance: Reinforcement pretraining (mid-training) objective.

items.title: Benchmarking Optimizers for Large Language Model Pretraining
items.tier_evidence: OpenReview forum fL9qDVnMJF: 'Submitted to NeurIPS 2025 Datasets and Benchmarks Track'; second forum Jw7khYzYzl; no proceedings entry found
items.one_sentence_method: Standardized tuning of 12 optimizers (AdamW, ADOPT, AdEMAMix, Lion, Signum, Muon, D-Muon, SOAP, Sophia, SF-AdamW, Prodigy, MARS) across batch size, model size and duration.
items.largest_scale_tested: 124M-720M, up to ~48B tokens, batch to 1M tokens
items.headline_claim: AdEMAMix and MARS best at 720M/1M-token batch; D-Muon consistent across settings; Sophia diverges at small batch; sign methods need large batch.
items.path_relevance: Optimizer benchmark complementary to Fantastic Optimizers.

items.title: Hybrid Architectures for Language Models: Systematic Analysis and Design Insights
items.tier_evidence: OpenReview forum 1aAFc4OANr: submitted to ICLR 2026 (2025-09-19, modified 2026-02-11); acceptance not confirmed
items.one_sentence_method: Holistic comparison of inter-layer vs intra-layer Transformer/Mamba hybrids on quality, long context, MoE compatibility, compute-optimal scaling and efficiency.
items.headline_claim: Hybrids beat homogeneous models by up to 2.9%; 1:1 ratio best quality, ~1:5 best trade-off; intra-layer hybrids best Pareto; hybrids scale between Transformer and Mamba.
items.path_relevance: Design rules for hybrid frontier architectures.

items.title: Navigating LLM Valley: From AdamW to Memory-Efficient and Matrix-Based Optimizers (survey)
items.tier_evidence: arXiv HTML header 'Submitted ... Under review' (journal-style template)
items.one_sentence_method: Survey organizing LLM optimizers into first-order, adaptive, memory-efficient, curvature-aware, sign-based, low-rank and matrix-based families with benchmarking methodology.
items.headline_claim: Argues optimizer research must move to scale-aware comparisons of convergence, stability, memory and implementation complexity.
items.path_relevance: Survey of optimizer families for pretraining.

items.title: Kimi K3: Open Frontier Intelligence
items.v1_date: 2026-07 (day not shown on fetched abs page)
items.one_sentence_method: 2.8T-parameter MoE with Kimi Delta Attention, Attention Residuals, Stable LatentMoE (16 of 896 experts), 1M context, perfectly balanced expert-parallel training.
items.headline_claim: ~2.5x overall scaling efficiency over Kimi K2; outperforms other open and proprietary models in its suite while trailing Claude Fable 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol.
items.path_relevance: Primary frontier evidence for KDA, AttnRes, latent MoE and balanced EP.
items.known_frontier_adoption: Kimi K3 itself; third-party blog reports Quantile Balancing used.

items.title: GLM-5: from Vibe Coding to Agentic Engineering
items.one_sentence_method: Adopts DeepSeek Sparse Attention to cut training/inference cost, plus asynchronous RL infrastructure.
items.largest_scale_tested: 744B total / ~40B active (per architecture card), 200K->1M context in GLM-5.2
items.headline_claim: DSA reduces training and inference cost while maintaining long-context fidelity; MuonSplit (per-head Muon) used per 2605.08933.
items.path_relevance: Frontier adoption of sparse attention and per-head Muon.

items.title: Muon is Scalable for LLM Training (Moonlight)
items.tier_evidence: Moonshot technical report; PMLR/OpenReview not found
items.one_sentence_method: Muon with weight decay and update-RMS matching to AdamW, ZeRO-1 distributed implementation.
items.headline_claim: ~2x computational efficiency vs AdamW at compute-optimal; update RMS 0.2 best.
items.path_relevance: Seed paper: first frontier-scale Muon recipe.

items.title: Kimi K2: Open Agentic Intelligence
items.one_sentence_method: MuonClip = Muon + weight decay + RMS matching + per-head QK-Clip rescaling of Wq/Wk when max attention logit exceeds tau=100.
items.largest_scale_tested: 1.04T total / 32B active MoE, 15.5T tokens, batch 67M tokens
items.headline_claim: Zero loss spikes over 15.5T tokens; vanilla Muon at 53B/9B active showed logits >1000.
items.path_relevance: Frontier Muon stability recipe.

items.title: Kimi Linear: An Expressive, Efficient Attention Architecture
items.tier_evidence: Moonshot technical report with open kernels/checkpoints
items.one_sentence_method: Kimi Delta Attention: Gated DeltaNet with channel-wise gating and a specialized DPLR chunkwise kernel, hybridized 3:1 with MLA (NoPE).
items.headline_claim: Outperforms full MLA under identical recipe; 75% less KV cache; up to 6x decode throughput at 1M context.
items.path_relevance: Hybrid linear attention for frontier pretraining.

items.title: Attention Residuals
items.one_sentence_method: Replaces unit-weight residual accumulation with softmax attention over preceding layer (or block) outputs using one pseudo-query per layer; Block AttnRes plus pipeline caching.
items.largest_scale_tested: Kimi Linear 48B/3B on 1.4T tokens; scaling-law sweeps
items.headline_claim: Block AttnRes matches a baseline trained with 1.25x more compute; <4% training and <2% inference overhead; shifts optimum to deeper models.
items.path_relevance: Depth-wise information flow (hyper-connection alternative).

items.title: mHC: Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections
items.tier_evidence: DeepSeek technical report; paperswithcode lists ICML 2026 but not verified on icml.cc
items.one_sentence_method: Projects hyper-connection residual mappings onto doubly-stochastic matrices via Sinkhorn-Knopp to restore identity-mapping stability, with fused kernels and DualPipe overlap.
items.headline_claim: Removes HC instabilities (Amax ~3000 -> ~1.6), +2.1 BBH/+2.3 DROP, 6.7% time overhead.
items.path_relevance: Hyper-connections made trainable at scale.

items.title: LatentMoE: Toward Optimal Accuracy per FLOP and Parameter in Mixture of Experts
items.one_sentence_method: Projects tokens to a latent dimension for routed-expert compute and dispatch, reinvesting d/l savings into more experts and higher top-k.
items.headline_claim: Consistently better accuracy per FLOP and per parameter than standard MoE; 8B/73B LatentMoE beats iso-size MoE on all tasks.
items.path_relevance: Latent MoE / Stable LatentMoE lineage.

items.title: DeepSeek-V3.2: Pushing the Frontier of Open Large Language Models
items.one_sentence_method: DeepSeek Sparse Attention: FP8 lightning indexer + top-2048 token selection under MLA (MQA mode), added by continued pretraining with indexer KL warm-up.
items.headline_claim: Core attention O(Lk) with near-identical benchmarks to V3.1-Terminus; large long-context cost reduction.
items.path_relevance: Production sparse attention.

items.title: Pretraining Large Language Models with NVFP4
items.one_sentence_method: NVFP4 pretraining recipe: random Hadamard transforms, 2D block scaling for weights, stochastic rounding for gradients, first/last blocks in BF16.
items.headline_claim: Loss within ~1-1.5% of FP8; MMLU-Pro 62.58 vs 62.62; each recipe component is necessary.
items.path_relevance: FP4 pretraining at multi-trillion-token horizon.

items.title: Nemotron 3 Super: Open, Efficient Mixture-of-Experts Hybrid Mamba-Transformer Model for Agentic Reasoning
items.one_sentence_method: 120B/12B-active hybrid Mamba-Attention LatentMoE pretrained in NVFP4 on 25T tokens with MTP layers and aux-loss-free sigmoid routing.
items.headline_claim: First production model pretrained in NVFP4; 2.2x-7.5x throughput vs GPT-OSS-120B/Qwen3.5-122B at comparable accuracy.
items.path_relevance: Frontier evidence for NVFP4 + LatentMoE + MTP.

items.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3: Efficient and Open Intelligence
items.one_sentence_method: Family white paper: hybrid Mamba-Transformer MoE, LatentMoE and NVFP4 for Super/Ultra, MTP layers, 1M context.
items.headline_claim: LatentMoE (8B/73B) beats standard MoE on all tasks at equal size; NVFP4 pretraining for larger models.
items.path_relevance: Frontier adoption summary.

items.title: SOAP, Muon, and Beyond: Pushing LLM Pretraining Scales
items.tier_evidence: NVIDIA technical report (Megatron-LM / Emerging-Optimizers open source)
items.one_sentence_method: Stabilizes SOAP at large batch (per-step QR, KL-Shampoo covariance) and compares AdamW, Muon and SOAP with update-RMS-matched learning rates.
items.largest_scale_tested: Up to 72B/8B-active LatentMoE and 30B/3B Nemotron-Nano-V3; 1-3T tokens; batch up to 100M tokens
items.headline_claim: Muon and SOAP keep token-efficient convergence at 100M-token batches where AdamW degrades; KL-SOAP slightly best; Muon should not be applied to Mamba conv1D weights.
items.path_relevance: Largest public Muon/SOAP-vs-AdamW study.

items.title: MiniMax-01: Scaling Foundation Models with Lightning Attention
items.one_sentence_method: Hybrid of lightning (linear) attention and softmax attention (7:1) with MoE, trained to 1M context and extrapolated to 4M.
items.headline_claim: Matches GPT-4o/Claude-3.5-class models with 20-32x longer context.
items.path_relevance: First frontier-scale hybrid linear attention model.

items.title: Qwen2.5-1M Technical Report
items.one_sentence_method: Progressive long-context pretraining 4K->32K->64K->128K->256K with ABF RoPE base increases and synthetic long-dependency data, then DCA extrapolation to 1M.
items.headline_claim: Training at 256K improves 128K RULER (83.8->87.6); DCA gives >80% passkey at 1M without 1M training.
items.path_relevance: 1M-token context training recipe.

items.title: From 128K to 4M: Efficient Training of Ultra-Long Context Large Language Models (UltraLong)
items.one_sentence_method: One-step continued pretraining to 1M/2M/4M with YaRN RoPE scaling, document separators without cross-document masking, TP=8 and context parallelism.
items.headline_claim: One-step extension beats multi-step (RULER 80.17 vs 77.52 at 1M); short-context accuracy preserved.
items.path_relevance: Million-token context training infrastructure.

items.title: BitNet b1.58 2B4T Technical Report
items.one_sentence_method: Native 1.58-bit (ternary weights, 8-bit activations) transformer trained from scratch.
items.headline_claim: On par with full-precision open models of similar size with 0.4GB memory and 29ms CPU latency.
items.path_relevance: Quantization-aware training from pretraining at extreme precision.

items.title: Dion: Distributed Orthonormalized Updates
items.one_sentence_method: Replaces Newton-Schulz with amortized power iteration on a decoupled momentum buffer, low-rank (rank-fraction) updates with error feedback, compatible with DDP/FSDP/TP sharding.
items.headline_claim: At 3B, rank d/4 matches full-rank Muon; larger models tolerate lower rank; far lower wall-clock at large matrix sizes.
items.path_relevance: Distributed Muon alternative.

items.title: Dion2: A Simple Method to Shrink Matrix in Muon
items.one_sentence_method: Selects a fraction of rows/columns (by norm) each step, orthonormalizes only those with error feedback, giving sparse cheaper updates.
items.headline_claim: Simpler than Dion with reduced computation and communication; recommended over Dion in microsoft/dion.
items.path_relevance: Distributed/scalable Muon.

items.title: Practical Efficiency of Muon for Pretraining
items.one_sentence_method: Compute-time Pareto analysis of Muon vs AdamW across batch sizes plus muP transfer with a telescoping sweep that shrinks the grid at each width doubling.
items.largest_scale_tested: 100M-4B, batch up to 16M tokens, 3.7B muP target
items.headline_claim: Muon needs 10-15% fewer tokens with the gap persisting beyond the critical batch size; muP transfers LR and weight decay with Muon up to 3.7B; O(C log N) tuning overhead.
items.path_relevance: Telescoping sweeps and muP-with-Muon.

items.title: Muon Optimizes Under Spectral Norm Constraints
items.tier_evidence: NeurIPS 2025 OPT workshop (neurips.cc/virtual/2025/124312, contributed talk); not main track
items.one_sentence_method: Places Muon in the Lion-K family (nuclear-norm K) and proves Muon with decoupled weight decay converges to KKT points of loss minimization under ||W||_op <= 1/lambda.
items.headline_claim: Muon+weight decay is a stochastic Frank-Wolfe method on a spectral-norm ball; weight decay sets the constraint radius.
items.path_relevance: Spectral/steepest-descent framing and weight-decay theory for Muon.

items.title: Spectral Allocation: Why Muon Outperforms Adam, and How to Improve Muon (SAMuon)
items.one_sentence_method: Out-of-sample spectral probing of momentum singular directions shows a volatile head at edge-of-stability and a tolerant bulk; SAMuon amplifies the bulk with a static prior via low-rank SVD or power iteration.
items.headline_claim: 13.3-24.0% fewer tokens than tuned Muon (Scion impl.) with no persistent extra state; gains grow with batch size.
items.path_relevance: Newest Muon variant / mechanism study.

items.title: Predictable Scale: Part I, Step Law -- Optimal Hyperparameter Scaling Law in LLM Pretraining
items.tier_evidence: OpenReview attachment id uyBxGEZVYX exists but venue not confirmed
items.one_sentence_method: Grid-search of LR and batch size over 3,700 runs to fit eta(N,D)=1.79 N^-0.713 D^0.307 and B(D)=0.58 D^0.571, validated across dense/MoE and data recipes.
items.largest_scale_tested: 3,700 runs, ~1M H800 hours, ~100T tokens; 6.5B MoE validation
items.headline_claim: Predicted optima within 0.094% of exhaustive-search loss; batch size depends on D only; loss landscape convex with broad optimum.
items.path_relevance: Hyperparameter scaling laws (LR, batch size).

items.title: IndexCache: Accelerating Sparse Attention via Cross-Layer Index Reuse
items.one_sentence_method: Partitions DSA layers into Full layers with indexers and Shared layers reusing the nearest Full layer's top-k indices; training-free greedy search or training-aware multi-layer distillation.
items.headline_claim: Removes 75% of indexer compute with negligible quality loss; 1.82x prefill and 1.48x decode speedup over DSA.
items.path_relevance: Seed paper: sparse-attention index sharing (IndexShare).
items.known_frontier_adoption: GLM-5.2 (IndexShare, four-layer full/shared pattern during mid-training) per third-party report.

items.title: A Systematic Analysis of Hybrid Linear Attention
items.affiliations: UC Santa Cruz; ByteDance Seed; others
items.one_sentence_method: Trains and releases 72 models (36 at 340M/20B tokens, 36 at 1.3B/100B tokens) across six linear-attention variants and five hybrid ratios.
items.headline_claim: Standalone quality does not predict hybrid quality; recall improves with more full-attention layers below 3:1; recommends HGRN-2 or GatedDeltaNet at 3:1-6:1.
items.path_relevance: Empirical design rules for hybrid ratios (matches Kimi Linear 3:1).

items.title: Scaling Latent Reasoning via Looped Language Models (Ouro)
items.affiliations: ByteDance Seed; UC Santa Cruz; Princeton; Mila; others
items.tier_evidence: No ICLR 2026 acceptance found on OpenReview/iclr.cc
items.one_sentence_method: Parameter-shared looped transformer pretrained with an entropy-regularized exit distribution over recurrent depths, then adaptive-exit gate training.
items.headline_claim: Match 4B and 8B standard transformers (2-3x parameter efficiency); gains come from knowledge manipulation, not capacity.
items.path_relevance: Looped/recurrent-depth pretraining at multi-trillion-token scale.

items.title: Reinforcement Pre-Training (RPT)
items.one_sentence_method: Reframes next-token prediction as next-token reasoning with on-policy RL and a prefix-matching verifiable reward on entropy-filtered positions.
items.headline_claim: Improves next-token accuracy to match a 32B model and shows power-law scaling with RL compute; but initialized from a reasoning model and math-only corpus.
items.path_relevance: Reinforcement pretraining objective (superseded by RLP).

items.title: Dream 7B: Diffusion Large Language Models
items.one_sentence_method: Masked diffusion LM initialized from Qwen2.5-7B with shift operation and context-adaptive token-level noise rescheduling.
items.headline_claim: Beats LLaDA 8B with 1/4 the data and excels at planning (Sudoku 81 vs 21 for Qwen2.5).
items.path_relevance: Diffusion LM (adapted, contrasts with from-scratch LLaDA).

items.title: Mercury: Ultra-Fast Language Models Based on Diffusion
items.tier_evidence: Commercial technical report; lab not on protocol's Tier-C list
items.one_sentence_method: Commercial-scale masked diffusion transformer trained on trillions of tokens with proprietary parallel-decoding engine.
items.headline_claim: 1109 tok/s (Mini) and 737 tok/s (Small) on H100, up to 10x faster than speed-optimized frontier models at comparable quality.
items.path_relevance: Production diffusion LM.

items.title: DLLM-JEPA: Joint Embedding Predictive Architectures for Masked Diffusion Language Models
items.one_sentence_method: Builds two JEPA views from one input via different masking rates in a masked diffusion LM, one gradient pass plus EMA target.
items.headline_claim: 33% fewer JEPA FLOPs than LLM-JEPA; up to +18.7pp GSM8K; pretraining left to future work.
items.path_relevance: JEPA objective for diffusion LMs (not yet pretraining).

items.title: BeyondWeb: Lessons from Scaling Synthetic Data for Trillion-scale Pretraining
items.tier_evidence: Company technical report; lab not on Tier-C list
items.one_sentence_method: Source-rephrasing synthetic data framework with quality-first seed selection, style matching and multi-format diversity.
items.headline_claim: +7.1pp over RedPajama and +2.6pp over Nemotron-Synth at 8B; 7.7x faster training; rephraser quality saturates at ~3B.
items.path_relevance: Rephrased/synthetic pretraining data.

items.title: PRISM: Demystifying Retention and Interaction in Mid-Training
items.one_sentence_method: Controlled mid-training (~27B tokens) across seven base models and two architecture types, followed by RL, with CKA/weight-change analysis.
items.headline_claim: +15-40 math, +5-12 code, +6-13 GPQA; mid-training restructures >90% of weights while RL changes ~5%; RL only succeeds after mid-training.
items.path_relevance: Mid-training design choices.

items.title: Predicting the Order of Upcoming Tokens Improves Language Modeling (TOP)
items.first_author_et_al: Zayd M. K. Zuhri et al.
items.one_sentence_method: Token Order Prediction: learning-to-rank auxiliary loss over proximity of upcoming tokens with one extra unembedding layer.
items.headline_claim: TOP beats both NTP and MTP on 8 benchmarks at all sizes; 7B MTP underperforms NTP on general tasks.
items.path_relevance: Alternative to MTP as auxiliary pretraining objective.

items.title: Breaking the Bubble: Asynchronous Pipeline Parallel Training with Bounded Weight Inconsistency (PACI)
items.one_sentence_method: Bubble-free asynchronous 1F1B where local gradient accumulation bounds forward/backward version drift without weight stashing or prediction.
items.headline_claim: Matches synchronous 1F1B-flush perplexity and memory with full utilization; up to 1.69x better time-to-accuracy.
items.path_relevance: Fully asynchronous pipeline training.

items.title: One-Step Gradient Delay is Not a Barrier for Large-Scale Asynchronous Pipeline Parallel LLM Pretraining
items.one_sentence_method: PipeDream-2BW constant one-step delay combined with delay-robust optimizers (Muon) and an error-feedback correction, with convergence analysis.
items.headline_claim: AdamW degrades under one-step delay but Muon is robust; Muon+EF matches synchronous final loss at 10B with identical hyperparameters.
items.path_relevance: Async pipelines interact with optimizer choice.

items.title: Quantile Balancing (QB) for MoE routing
items.first_author_et_al: Jianlin Su (method); Larry Dial / Marin team (validation)
items.tier_evidence: Blog posts and a Megatron-LM pull request (#5349); no arXiv paper found
items.one_sentence_method: Hyperparameter-free aux-loss-free balancing: after each step solve for per-token activation thresholds and per-expert biases (dual quantile update) that would have balanced load, apply next step.
items.largest_scale_tested: 32B-A5B on 326B tokens (1e22 FLOPs) on Marin; 1e23 underway
items.headline_claim: Zero loss spikes, no leading dense layers or auxiliary losses needed; outperforms fixed-increment bias + aux loss.
items.path_relevance: Ultra-sparse MoE load balancing.
items.known_frontier_adoption: Kimi K3 (per third-party blog); Megatron-LM implementation.

items.title: A Survey on Diffusion Language Models
items.one_sentence_method: Taxonomy of continuous/discrete DLMs, pretraining and post-training strategies, inference optimizations and multimodal extensions.
items.headline_claim: Highlights efficiency, long-sequence handling and infrastructure as open challenges.
items.path_relevance: Survey (diffusion LMs).

items.title: Discrete Diffusion in Large Language and Multimodal Models: A Survey
items.one_sentence_method: Systematic survey of dLLMs/dMLLMs: math, modeling, training, inference, quantization, applications.
items.headline_claim: Positions discrete diffusion as an alternative with up to 10x decoding speedups.
items.path_relevance: Survey (diffusion LMs).

items.title: Blog: Survey of Optimizers
items.one_sentence_method: Organizes 2025-2026 optimizers along temporal estimation, update geometry, horizon management and representation/systems axes.
items.headline_claim: Concludes there is no context-independent replacement for AdamW; rankings change with scale, D/N, batch, schedule and tuning budget.
items.path_relevance: Survey (optimizers).

items.title: Cautious Optimizers: Improving Training with One Line of Code [BASELINE, v1 outside window]
items.tier_evidence: OpenReview 'ICLR 2026 Poster' (forum zBPZeRjfgu); v1 predates window so recorded as baseline only
items.one_sentence_method: Masks momentum-optimizer updates whose sign disagrees with the current gradient.
items.headline_claim: Claimed up to 1.47x sample efficiency on Llama-1B; Fantastic Optimizers finds only a small lift.
items.path_relevance: Baseline for Cautious/variance-reduced Adam family.

open_problems.quote: 'While the exact reason for the speedup decay is not clear, we conjecture that the landscape-adaptation advantage of matrix-based optimizers plays a smaller role at the largest model scale we tested'; fitted law 'predicts that Muon will result in a slightly higher loss than AdamW in the 7B and 1x Chinchilla regime.'

'We conduct our benchmarking experiments on models of up to 720M parameters ... training behavior may change further at practical scales and with extremely long training durations. Especially when certain optimizers are not widely supported by modern sharding frameworks.'

muP 'can fail to model expressive preconditioners even at initialization' (SOAP); 'the compute optimal model size is larger for matrix-preconditioned optimizers compared to Adam' - untested beyond 1.4B.
'Our empirical tests were conducted on models with up to 1.5B non-embedding parameters. In future work, we plan to train large, state-of-the-art LLMs that leverage CompleteP.'
Answers 'the open question posed by Moonshot (2025) ... does the maximal-update parametrization (muP) remain valid when used together with Muon?' only up to 3.7B parameters.
'further investigation is required, including into how and when to adjust hyperparameters such as weight decay, batch size, and learning rate, in the high-TPP context.'
'finer-grained configuration decisions, such as model depth and context length, should be considered along with N, D, and B'; inference cost as a first-class Pareto objective.
Preconditioned methods 'face scalability hurdles when applied to large frontier models like fine-grained MoEs'; authors 'discuss the limitations of our conclusions' (SOAP memory and sharding).
'we lack a complete mechanistic explanation for why exactly higher momentum improves robustness. Additionally, our {batch size, learning rate} grids are restricted to the 135M model.'
'A more comprehensive comparison with DeMO is left for future work'; repo expects 'that 1/8, 1/16, and perhaps lower rank fractions will work well at 10B+ scale' (untested).
QB 'is robust across all tested compute scales up to 1e22 FLOPs (with 1e23 underway)'; 'The current QB implementation is a one-step approximation based on the prior step's routing scores.'

'the framework accommodates the exploration of diverse manifold constraints ... further investigation into distinct geometric constraints could yield novel methods that better optimize the trade-off between plasticity and stability.'
'finer-grained blocking remains a promising direction as future hardware constraints relax' (Block AttnRes uses ~8 blocks for memory reasons).

'the underlying reasons behind this seemingly counterintuitive observation [hybrids beating full attention] remain largely unexplored ... particularly as models push towards multi-million-token context lengths.'
'Future work could explore hybrid models that integrate the strengths of both [linear and sparse attention]' (Kimi K3 later combines KDA with MLA only).
Recipes 'could be checked at much larger scales to see whether the critical elements remain stable' (paper trained <=1B on 60B tokens).
'A natural next step is to test the findings at much larger scales and with more diverse domains ... how midtraining ... interact[s] with reinforcement learning based posttraining.'
'whether the same ordering [of mid-training timing] holds across larger models or different architectures remains an open question.'

'Our experiments are primarily conducted using a 14B parameter model ... corpus predominantly consists of mathematical documents ... investigating RPT training from a standard base language model would provide further insights.'

'direct comparisons between LLaDA and ARMs ... were restricted to a computational budget of less than 10^23 FLOPs ... both the model scale and the amount of training data for LLaDA remain smaller than those of leading ARM counterparts.'
'while EBTs scale well up to 800M parameters, we have not explored larger models due to resource constraints.'
'While our experiments mostly focus on finetuning, preliminary pretraining experiment are promising which we plan to scale and more thoroughly test in future work.'
'Future directions include applying DLLM-JEPA at pre-training.'
Optimizer research must move 'from single-algorithm speedup claims toward rigorous, scale-aware comparisons that jointly evaluate convergence, stability, memory, and implementation complexity.'
'there is no context-independent replacement for AdamW. Rankings change with model scale, data-to-parameter ratio, batch size, schedule, parameter partition, tuning budget, and ... target metric.'
DLM 'limitations and challenges ... including efficiency, long-sequence handling, and infrastructure requirements.'

negative_results.finding: Optimizer speedups over well-tuned AdamW shrink from 1.4x (0.1B) to ~1.1x (1.2B) with no downstream gain; many claimed 2x speedups reflect weak baselines; Muon is overtaken by Soap/Kron at >=8x Chinchilla.
Sophia diverges at small batch beyond the Chinchilla horizon even with lower LR; SF-AdamW, Lion and Signum scale poorly; vanilla Muon (no weight decay on 2D params) degrades with model size.
Under standard parameterization the Muon/SOAP/Shampoo advantage vanishes with width; muP alone fails the SOAP coordinate check without blocking or spectral normalization.
Vanilla Muon on a 53B/9B-active MoE drives attention logits above 1000 (instability), motivating QK-Clip.
Applying Muon to Mamba conv1D weights hurts convergence (fall back to AdamW); SOAP shows loss spikes at large batch without per-step QR / KL covariance.
A 7B MTP model underperforms NTP on standard NLP benchmarks (MTP gains do not extend beyond code).
Unconstrained hyper-connections show severe instability at scale (Amax magnitude ~3000) and extra memory traffic.
HALO and Jetfire become unstable when ported to FP4; LSS-INT4 diverges beyond ~50 tokens/param.
Removing any of stochastic rounding, Hadamard transforms, 2D weight scaling or the BF16 first/last blocks worsens the 12B/10T NVFP4 run.
Beyond a 'critical data size', adding training tokens increases loss in low-precision FP training.
W4A4 QAT quantization error rises with more training tokens and coarser groups; FC2 activation outliers are the bottleneck.
Distillation cannot beat supervised pretraining given enough compute; training a teacher for a single student is worse than supervised learning.
Standard data-constrained recipes (more epochs or parameters) eventually overfit; weight decay 0.1 is 30x too small.
Masked diffusion needs up to ~16x more compute than AR in the single-epoch regime; AR overfits at high epoch counts.
Naive LLM 'continuation' of web documents barely beats repeating data; high-quality seed data alone is insufficient.
Independent review (pith.science) notes no matched standard-NTP control on the same corpus; the continual-NTP baseline collapsed 51.2->10.7.
Micro-batch load-balancing loss suppresses expert specialization; switching to global-batch mid-training never fully recovers from-scratch performance.
Placing hybrid blocks only at the ends of the network (sandwich) causes large quality drops; hybrids without normalization are unstable.
The original PipeDream schedule degrades by >0.03 loss at 16 stages even with Muon+error feedback; only constant-delay 2BW scales.
Fully head-wise MuonSplit leads early but is overtaken by full-matrix Muon later in training.
Static MTP hurts small (1.3B-3B) models; curricula are needed.
